authorization: Researcher prioritizes decoding phase transitions and correction thresholds in the continuing Lab 008 study.
question: Can fractional matching or mass transport on the charge-matched single-path switching graph avoid deterministic-selector collisions and yield a size-uniform midpoint paired mass?
earliest_gate: Keep vertices as original binary currents and edges as one charge-preserving residual rough-to-rough path flip. Fractional weights must be symmetric across the flip and may not use hidden information beyond the current configuration used in the proof.
alternatives: Prove a size-uniform fractional capacity on a positive-probability RSW event, yielding a nonzero midpoint Bayes LER.
Show exact path-switching graphs have an intrinsic Hall/capacity deficit, closing single-path mass transport as a lower-bound route.
Show finite path-switching matchings are adequate but the asymptotic step requires a separately stated crossing-cluster or arm-event tail theorem.
planned_steps: Build the exact bipartite graph within each physical charge record, connecting opposite sectors only when one simple residual rough-to-rough path flip maps the currents.
Compute exact integral maximum matching and a symmetric fractional-flow certificate on L3 and L4; compare covered pairs with the Bayes numerator and the extremal-selector stable subset.
Audit whether path count, crossing-cluster count, or an arm event controls the required capacities; ordinary crossing probability alone is insufficient.
Stop without a threshold claim unless a size-uniform analytic probability/capacity bound is proved.
stop_rule: Stop at a finite Hall/capacity obstruction, exact saturation plus an explicit missing asymptotic theorem, or a proved size-uniform paired-mass bound. Do not expand beyond L4 or replace an analytic bound with two-size extrapolation.

observed.integral_fractional_relation: the integral matching is an optimal symmetric fractional certificate by bipartite matching-polytope integrality
observed.dual_certificate: the union of each charge record's smaller sector is a vertex cover of the same size
observed.decision: exact finite saturation; no all-size Hall theorem or size-uniform matching-density bound
